description: Windows is a Graphical User Interface (GUI) based Operating System developed by Microsoft. It is the most widely used operating system for personal computers (PCs) across the world, making it a crucial topic for computer awareness.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Windows OS
sections.description: Fundamental technical terminology essential for understanding the core operations of the Windows OS.

key_concepts.explanation: A system software that acts as an interface between computer hardware and the user, managing both hardware and software resources.
A visual interface that allows users to interact with the computer seamlessly using graphical elements like icons, menus, and pointers.
The default proprietary file system used by modern Windows versions to store, organize, and retrieve files on a hard drive.
The core component of the operating system that directly interacts with the hardware, managing memory, CPU time, and system resources.

sections.title: Historical Evolution of Windows Versions
sections.description: A chronological overview of major Windows versions released by Microsoft and their defining milestones.

historical_events.significance: Microsoft launched its first graphical operating environment. It heavily relied on MS-DOS for core functions.
Introduced the iconic 'Start Button' and 'Taskbar' for the first time. It also brought native Plug and Play support.
Renowned for its stability and improved user interface. It was the first consumer-oriented version built on the robust Windows NT architecture.
A highly successful version featuring the transparent Aero interface and significantly improved overall performance.
Introduced the 'One Windows' universal app concept, the Cortana virtual assistant, and the new Microsoft Edge browser.
The latest major iteration featuring a centered Start Menu, Snap Layouts for multitasking, and native support for Android applications.

sections.title: Key Components and Features of Windows OS
sections.description: Crucial tools, utilities, and security features integrated into the Microsoft Windows Operating System.

key_concepts.explanation: A panel usually located at the bottom of the screen that displays active programs, pinned apps, system tray icons, and the Start Menu.
A legacy user interface component that allows users to view and modify system settings (gradually being replaced by the modern 'Settings' app).
The built-in, comprehensive antivirus and anti-malware security program provided natively in modern Windows OS.
A temporary RAM storage area where copied or cut data (text, images, files) is held before being pasted elsewhere.
An integrated AI-powered assistant in Windows 11 designed to enhance productivity by answering queries and automating OS tasks.

sections.title: Important Windows Shortcut Keys

sections.title: Important Facts related to Windows
sections.description: Exam-oriented one-liner static facts regarding the Windows Operating System and its history.

important_facts.fact: The Windows OS was developed by Microsoft, a multinational technology corporation founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975.
Early Windows versions (like Windows 1.0 to 3.1) were not complete operating systems themselves, but rather graphical operating environments running on top of MS-DOS.
The Windows NT (New Technology) kernel architecture forms the foundational basis of all modern Windows OS versions, providing advanced security, multi-threading, and networking support.
Currently, Windows completely dominates the global PC market, with the vast majority of the world's desktop and laptop computers running on it.
